summary: VitalOrbit is an autonomous real-time astronaut health monitoring web application that tracks radiation exposure, cardiovascular fitness, musculoskeletal health, behavioral well-being, immune function, and habitat environment—empowering deep-space crews to detect early physiological shifts, execute guided self-assessments, and trigger evidence-based countermeasures independently during long communication delays with Earth.
details:
THE CHALLENGE & INSPIRATION

Long-duration missions to the Moon, Mars, and beyond expose astronauts to the five primary hazards of human spaceflight: space radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, altered gravity fields, and hostile/closed environments. On these deep-space voyages, multi-minute communication latencies prevent real-time clinical intervention from ground flight surgeons. Astronauts must take primary responsibility for monitoring their own health, spotting early physiological deterioration, and initiating countermeasures before minor issues become catastrophic emergencies.

WHAT VITALORBIT DOES

VitalOrbit is an autonomous, browser-based physiological telemetry and environmental monitoring system built specifically for deep-space crews. It consolidates six physiological and environmental domains into a cohesive, mission-critical dashboard:

1. Radiation Dosimetry: Tracks cumulative career dose (against NASA's 1,000 mSv career REIC standard), daily exposure rates, and organ-equivalent doses (blood-forming organs, eye lens, skin, and central nervous system). It provides space weather tracking and Solar Particle Event (SPE) storm-shelter advisories based on Canadian Space Agency (CSA) dosimetry research.

2. Cardiovascular & Hemodynamics: Features a live 500 Hz animated Lead-II ECG waveform, resting heart rate, non-invasive blood pressure, continuous heart rate variability (rMSSD) reflecting autonomic nervous tone, VO2 max trend tracking, and an interactive 3-minute Orthostatic Intolerance Protocol to assess post-microgravity cardiovascular deconditioning.

3. Musculoskeletal Health: Monitors regional Bone Mineral Density (BMD) loss across the lumbar spine, femoral neck, and wrist alongside lean muscle mass index. It tracks compliance against NASA's mandatory 2.5-hour/day exercise prescription across ARED (resistance loading), T2 (treadmill), and CEVIS (cycle ergometer).

4. Behavioral Health & Sleep Architecture: Combines continuous actigraphy sleep stage breakdown (Deep N3, Light, REM, Awake), daily psychological mood tracking, an embedded PHQ-2 depression screener, an on-board reaction-time test (WinSCAT PVT), and an encrypted private mission journal.

5. Immune Competence & Biomarkers: Surfaces on-board hematology metrics (WBC differential breakdown, neutrophils, lymphocytes), systemic inflammation markers (hs-CRP, IL-6), and salivary PCR latent virus reactivation surveillance (EBV, VZV, CMV) to preempt immune dysregulation.

6. Habitat Environment (ECLSS): Monitors cabin partial pressure of CO2 (ppCO2 with active CDRA scrubber cycle controls), atmospheric pressure, internal temperature, relative humidity, acoustic levels, and water reclamation potability.

7. Autonomous Self-Assessment Wizard: An interactive clinical decision-support engine featuring Visual Analog Scales (VAS) for headache, nausea, and fatigue, body symptom tagging, and a Space Flight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS) near-vision screener. Submitting an assessment generates clinical severity scoring and evidence-based countermeasure protocols.

HOW IT WORKS

VitalOrbit is built with clean HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript, leveraging Chart.js for data visualization. It requires zero server backend, runs client-side, operates completely offline in spacecraft cabins, and supports one-click JSON clinical telemetry export for ground synchronization.
